source.title: Low-power multi-mode fiber projector overcomes shallow neural networks classifiers
source.authors: D. Ancora; M. Negri; A. Gianfrate; D. Trypogeorgos; L. Dominici; D. Sanvitto; F. Ricci-Tersenghi; Luca Leuzzi

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether a perturbation-based flatness measure tracks test accuracy across shallow classifiers trained on different projected datasets. This is a conceptual test related to V7, using a different model family and setting.
record.gate_note: The study reports MNIST classification accuracy and local-energy profiles for several input representations. It does not test fitting random labels, width beyond interpolation, convolutional versus fully connected classifiers, optimizer or batch-size effects, dropout, or removal of memorized examples. Values used to describe some dataset comparisons are in figures; no exact values are reconstructed from those plots.
record.test_reason: The study examines a related flatness–test-accuracy relationship in logistic classifiers across input representations. It does not test V7's ranking of train–test gaps within a convolutional family trained to similarly low loss, or any other listed version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially accurate. The authors find that physical MMF projections improve logistic-classifier test accuracy over raw images and comparison transformations. They conjecture that flatter local-energy profiles help explain this advantage, acknowledge the upscaled-versus-simulated exception, and describe local energy as only an approximation to local entropy.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains a logistic regression readout on experimentally measured or simulated fiber projections of MNIST, rather than testing the listed standard deep-network training recipes or measuring magnitude-aware sharpness in a convolutional family.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report that the upscaled and simulated datasets share a local-energy profile despite different test accuracy. Experiment 2 also reports that strong β-camera underexposure has only a marginally negative effect on classification performance.

fits_no_version.finding: Measured MMF representations yield flatter multiplicative-noise training-error profiles and higher test accuracy in logistic classifiers. Upscaled and simulated representations have equal profiles despite different test accuracy.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Across these MNIST representations, multiplicative-noise robustness of logistic readouts broadly correlates with test accuracy, with an explicit exception.

record.problems: The evidence concerns a shallow logistic classifier on a fraction of MNIST, not the deep-network conditions in most claim versions. Hyperparameters were not tuned. The local-energy measure is described as only an approximation to local entropy, and the upscaled-versus-simulated comparison is an explicit exception to the reported correlation. Several profiles and accuracy comparisons are figure-based without exact values in the supplied text.

untested.parts: Fitting fixed random labels and comparing natural-label versus random-label held-out accuracy.
Widening beyond a demonstrated zero-training-error threshold; changing output resolution does not establish this condition.
Own experimental comparisons of convolutional and fully connected networks and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus SGD optimizers under specified tuning regimes.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout comparisons and its interactions with training-set size, augmentation, and weight decay.

Generalization-gap ranking within a convolutional family at similarly low training loss, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures. Multiplicative parameter noise is measured, but against test accuracy across different representations.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equal-sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for any listed version. Its citations to convolutional accuracy and V7's original source do not supply its own tests of those versions.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural versus random labels.
Network width beyond the threshold for zero training error.
Comparison of convolutional and fully connected networks on images.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and the effects of tuning or weight decay.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations to the training recipe.
Dropout and its interaction with training-set size, data augmentation, and weight decay.

The study uses shallow logistic classifiers and compares input representations, not one convolutional family trained to similarly low loss. It does not compare against the tested norm- and margin-based measures or test magnitude-aware sharpness across model families.
Removing memorized training examples and comparing with random removals.

rows.subject: logistic classifier trained on MMF α-cam speckles
rows.size_stated: 10 classes; output space N = 900 × 900 in the described architecture
rows.operation_detail: Measured the local energy by adding multiplicative Gaussian noise to model parameters and computing training misclassification; compared its profile with test accuracy.
rows.measure: Local energy profile (fraction of misclassified training points as multiplicative noise increases), related to test accuracy.
rows.value: The authors describe the MMF solutions as having very low local-energy variation and profiles stable up to noise of the order of 10 times the signal-to-noise ratio; they report better test accuracy for MMF data than for the direct MNIST set.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars show the standard deviation over 30 samples.
rows.locator: Results and discussions, “Accuracy of random projections and behavior of the training error”; Fig. 3
rows.note: The stated relation is qualitative; no exact local-energy or test-accuracy values are given in the text for this condition.
rows.check: The reported robustness and higher test accuracy concern a logistic readout across representations, not V7's controlled comparison of convolutional-network generalization gaps.

rows.subject: logistic classifier trained on MMF β-cam speckles
rows.size_stated: 10 classes; output space N = 900 × 900 in the described architecture
rows.operation_detail: Measured the local energy by adding multiplicative Gaussian noise to model parameters and computing training misclassification; compared its profile with test accuracy.
rows.measure: Local energy profile (fraction of misclassified training points as multiplicative noise increases), related to test accuracy.
rows.value: The authors describe the MMF solutions as having very low local-energy variation and profiles stable up to noise of the order of 10 times the signal-to-noise ratio; they report better test accuracy for MMF data than for the direct MNIST set.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars show the standard deviation over 30 samples.
rows.locator: Results and discussions, “Accuracy of random projections and behavior of the training error”; Fig. 3
rows.note: The study says α- and β-camera classification performance is identical in experiment 1; it does not give separate exact local-energy values in the text.
rows.check: The reported robustness and higher test accuracy do not establish V7's gap-ranking effect. Experiment 2's strongly underexposed β-camera also performs slightly worse than α-camera.

rows.subject: logistic classifier trained on simulated MMF α-simulated speckles
rows.size_stated: 10 classes; output space N = 900 × 900 in the described architecture
rows.operation_detail: Measured the local energy by adding multiplicative Gaussian noise to model parameters and computing training misclassification; compared its profile with test accuracy.
rows.measure: Local energy profile (fraction of misclassified training points as multiplicative noise increases), related to test accuracy.
rows.value: The authors say the simulated dataset has the same local-energy profile as upscaled MNIST, and its test accuracy is below the measured MMF data.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars show the standard deviation over 30 samples.
rows.locator: Results and discussions, “Accuracy of random projections and behavior of the training error”; Fig. 3
rows.note: The text does not provide exact profile or accuracy values for this condition.
rows.check: Matching another representation's local-energy profile is not a partial occurrence of V7. Neither comparable low training loss nor the train–test-gap ranking is established.

rows.subject: logistic classifier trained on upscaled MNIST
rows.size_stated: 10 classes; input set resized to L = 600 in experiment 1
rows.operation_detail: Measured the local energy by adding multiplicative Gaussian noise to model parameters and computing training misclassification; compared its profile with test accuracy.

conditions.value: experiment 2 for local-energy comparison; experiment 1 uses L = 600

rows.measure: Local energy profile (fraction of misclassified training points as multiplicative noise increases), related to test accuracy.
rows.value: The authors state that its local-energy profile matches the simulated dataset, but its test accuracy is lower.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars show the standard deviation over 30 samples.
rows.locator: Results and discussions, “Accuracy of random projections and behavior of the training error”; Fig. 3
rows.note: This is an explicit exception to the reported relationship between flatter profiles and higher test accuracy.
rows.check: Equal local-energy profiles with unequal test accuracy are an exception to the paper's broader correlation, not evidence that V7 is absent. The experiment-1 resolution should not be assigned to the experiment-2 profile without confirmation.

rows.subject: logistic classifier trained on randomized MNIST
rows.size_stated: 10 classes; randomized set sized to match the fiber output dimension
rows.operation_detail: Measured the local energy by adding multiplicative Gaussian noise to model parameters and computing training misclassification; compared its profile with test accuracy.

conditions.value: experiment 1; up to 9000 training examples; L = 600

rows.measure: Local energy profile (fraction of misclassified training points as multiplicative noise increases), related to test accuracy.
rows.value: The paper reports that MMF-transformed data has higher test accuracy than randomized MNIST; the precise profile comparison is shown in Fig. 3.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars show the standard deviation over 30 samples.
rows.note: The supplied text does not describe the randomized-MNIST local-energy result precisely enough to assign the direction of the profile comparison.
rows.check: Figure 3 uses models trained on 3800 examples, not the stated experiment-1 condition of up to 9000. Randomized MNIST means random input projection, not random labels; this tests neither V1 nor V7.

rows.subject: logistic classifier trained on original MNIST
rows.operation_detail: Measured the local energy by adding multiplicative Gaussian noise to model parameters and computing training misclassification; compared its profile with test accuracy.
rows.measure: Local energy profile (fraction of misclassified training points as multiplicative noise increases), related to test accuracy.
rows.value: The paper reports that MMF-transformed data has higher test accuracy than the direct MNIST set; the precise profile comparison is shown in Fig. 3.
rows.uncertainty: Error bars show the standard deviation over 30 samples.
rows.note: The supplied text does not describe the original-MNIST local-energy result precisely enough to assign the direction of the profile comparison.
rows.check: Figure 3 uses reference models trained on 3800 examples; the row incorrectly attaches experiment-1 training counts. Its test-accuracy comparison does not measure V7's controlled gap ranking.
